Use the `--workers` option. When deploying applications you will probably want to have some **replication of processes** to take advantage of **multiple cores** and to be able to handle more requests.[2] You can start multiple workers with the `--workers` command line option[3].

**With the `fastapi` command:**

```console
$ fastapi run --workers 4 main.py
```

**With `uvicorn` directly:**

```console
$ uv run uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --workers 4
```

The only new option here is `--workers` telling Uvicorn to start 4 worker processes.[4] In the output, it shows the **PID** of each process, `27365` for the parent process (this is the **process manager**) and one for each worker process[4].

**If you use containers:** when running on **Kubernetes** you will probably **not** want to use workers and instead run **a single Uvicorn process per container**[2]. In that setup, you would already be handling replication at the cluster level.[5]

Of course, there are **special cases** where you could want to have **a container** with several **Uvicorn worker processes** inside.[5] One example is when you could be deploying to a **single server** (not a cluster) with **Docker Compose**[5]. In that case, set the workers in your Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
CMD ["fastapi", "run", "app/main.py", "--port", "80", "--workers", "4"]
```
